title: Replace detailed Hunch instructions with minimal MCP-delegate grounding block
context: The grounding block in editor rules (.cursor/hunch.mdc) previously contained extensive inline instructions covering all Hunch workflows (task start, context lookup, constraints, reporting). This was verbose and duplicated information available through MCP tools.
decision: Regenerated the grounding block to be minimal — one summary statement and a pointer to `hunch_*` MCP tools, removing ~40 lines of prescriptive instructions. Users now discover workflows through tool documentation rather than inline hints.
consequences: Grounding block is concise, reducing initial cognitive load in editor rules
Users must call MCP tools or read their help to discover workflows (learning curve shift)
Single source of truth for Hunch workflows moves from editor rules to MCP tool layer
All four edited files (.github/copilot-instructions.md, .windsurf/rules/hunch.md, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) likely received similar regeneration, keeping grounding blocks consistent across IDE rule sets
alternatives_rejected: Keep full detailed inline instructions (too verbose for rules files)
Remove Hunch context entirely (loses discovery and initial orientation)
Maintain separate instructions per IDE rule file (inconsistent, harder to maintain)
